```{r}
complete_ruggedness_df$rugg <- abs(complete_ruggedness_df$rugg)
complete_ruggedness_df$landscape_ID <- interaction(complete_ruggedness_df$n, complete_ruggedness_df$k, complete_ruggedness_df$c, complete_ruggedness_df$IM_rep, complete_ruggedness_df$scape_rep)

for (i in 1:nrow(peaks_total_ranked2_summarised[, ])){
```

## Network representation of adaptive walks
```{r}
# Making an adjacency matrix (which metagenotypes can mutate into each other?)
x <- as.data.frame(gtools::permutations(2, 4, c(1:2), repeats = TRUE))
x$ID <- 1:16

adj_mat <- matrix(16, 16, data = rep(0, 16^2))

for (i in 1:16) {
  
  adj_mat[i,findNeighbours(x, i, 4)$ID] <- 1
  
}


# translating my adaptive walks into something I can use here
# I need to extract the transitions from my adaptive walks -> format: from - to - in how many replicates of walk

walks_dfs <- NULL
for (i in 1:48){
  
 temp_df <- peaks_nkcs_2011[[5]][[1]][[1]][[26]][[3]][[i]] # true walk
 
 IDs <- NULL
 
 for (j in 0:max(temp_df[[1]][,"step"])) {
   
    metagenotype <- temp_df[[1]][temp_df[[1]]$step == j, c("F.1", "F.2", "P.1", "P.2")]
 ID_temp <- x[rowSums(mapply(`==`, x[, c("V1", "V2", "V3", "V4")], metagenotype)) == 4, "ID"] # extract the ID of the metagenotype that matches my adjacency matrix IDs
 
 IDs <- c(IDs, ID_temp)
   
 }
 
 from_IDs <- IDs[1:(length(IDs)-1)]
 to_IDs <- IDs[2:length(IDs)]
 
 temp_df <- data.frame(from = from_IDs,
                       to = to_IDs,
                      step = temp_df[[1]][c(2:nrow(temp_df[[1]])),"step"],
                       focal = temp_df[[1]][c(2:nrow(temp_df[[1]])),"focal"],
                       walk = i)
 
 walks_dfs <- rbind(walks_dfs, temp_df)
  
}

walks_dfs_summed <- as.data.frame(walks_dfs |> 
                            dplyr::group_by(from, to, focal, walk) |>
                            dplyr::summarise(step_count = n()))

walks_dfs_summed2 <- as.data.frame(walks_dfs_summed |> 
                            dplyr::group_by(from, to, focal) |>
                            dplyr::summarise(rep_count = n())) # this gives me in how many replicates certain steps were taken from x to y given a certain focal species


g <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(walks_dfs_summed2, 
                           directed = TRUE)

# add metadata to the nodes in the network (here "averaged per node")
igraph::V(g)$count <- ave(walks_dfs_summed2$rep_count, walks_dfs_summed2$from, FUN = max)[match(V(g)$name, walks_dfs_summed2$from)]

ranks_sp1 <- peaks_nkcs_2011[[4]][[1]][[1]][[26]][[1]]$rank
test_df <- peaks_nkcs_2011[[4]][[1]][[1]][[26]][[2]]
ranks_sp2 <- test_df[order(test_df$P.1, test_df$P.2, test_df$F.1, test_df$F.2), "rank"]

igraph::V(g)$rank_sp1 <- ranks_sp1
igraph::V(g)$rank_sp2 <- ranks_sp2


graph <- ggraph::ggraph(g,
               layout = "stress") +
  geom_edge_fan(aes(linetype = as.factor(focal)), # different edge color for the different steps based on focal species
                 end_cap = circle(5, "mm"), # buffer between node and arrow
                colour = "grey40") + 
  geom_edge_fan(arrow = arrow(type = "closed", # make arrow heads separately so they all have solid outlines
                              angle = 20, # "width" of arrow tip
                              length = unit(4, "mm")), # length of arrow tip
                edge_width = 0,
                 end_cap = circle(5, "mm"), # buffer between node and arrow
                colour = "grey40") + 
  geom_edge_loop(aes(linetype = as.factor(focal),
                     strength = (3*focal/4)), # to make non-overlapping loops
                 end_cap = circle(4, "mm"),
                colour = "grey40") +
  geom_edge_loop(aes(strength = (3*focal/4)), # make arrow heads separately so they all have solid outlines
                 arrow = arrow(type = "closed",
                               angle = 20,
                 length = unit(4, "mm")),
                 edge_width = 0,
                 end_cap = circle(4, "mm"),
                colour = "grey40") +
  geom_node_arc_bar(aes(x0 = x,
                        y0 = y,
                        r0 = 0, 
                        r = count/300 + 0.1,
                       start = pi, 
                       end = 2*pi,
                       fill = rank_sp1),
                       colour = "white") + # left semicircle
  geom_node_arc_bar(aes(x0 = x,
                        y0 = y,
                        r0 = 0, 
                        r = count/300 + 0.1, 
                        start = 0, 
                        end = pi,
                       fill = rank_sp2),
                       colour = "white") + # right semicircle
  #geom_node_text(aes(label = name)) +                   # "name" is automatically generated from the node IDs in the edges; then adjust r0 o read text
  scale_size(range = c(5, 15),
             guide = "none") +
  scale_edge_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "dashed"),
                             name = "focal species") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(name = "fitness rank",
                         low = "#5d36f7",
                         high = "#f9db45",
                         mid = "#f274f0",
                         midpoint = mean(ranks_sp1), # to adjust midpoint for landscapes with more or less peaks
                         guide = "colourbar",
                         aesthetics = "fill",
                         transform = "reverse",
                       breaks = c(1, 4, 8, 12, 16)) +
  theme_void() +
  guides(edge_linetype = guide_legend(position = "top"))

graph

```

```{r}

# figure out number of potential peaks for each landscape replicate
peaks_replicated <- NULL

for (rep in 1:4) {

for(scape in 1:50){
  
  scape_sp1 <- peaks_nkcs_2111[[4]][[1]][[rep]][[scape]][[1]] # take desired landscape replicate for species 1 = "focal species"

# rename columns, so I can combine the landscapes of both species next
colnames(scape_sp1)[c(7,8)] <- c("fitness_sp1", "rank_sp1")

# take the corresponding fitness landscape of species 2 in the chosen species pair
scape_sp2 <- peaks_nkcs_2111[[4]][[1]][[rep]][[scape]][[2]]
scape_sp2 <- scape_sp2[with(scape_sp2, order(P.1, P.2, F.1, F.2)), ] # reordering the loci, so they are in the same order as for sp 1

# combine landscaps of sp1 and sp2
scapes_combined <- cbind(scape_sp1, scape_sp2[,c(7,8)])
colnames(scapes_combined)[c(9,10)] <- c("fitness_sp2", "rank_sp2") # adjust column names

# get the metagenotypes, so I can plot them; this is just for text in the plot
for (i in 1:16){
  
  scapes_combined$seq[i] <- paste(paste(scapes_combined[i, c("F.1", "F.2")], collapse = ""), "-", c(paste(scapes_combined[i, c("P.1", "P.2")], collapse = "")))
  
}

scapes_combined$background <- paste0(scapes_combined$P.1, scapes_combined$P.2) # genotype of sp2
scapes_combined$gen <- paste0(scapes_combined$F.1, scapes_combined$F.2) # genotype of sp1

# now I use my function from the NKC(S) code file to infer which metagenotypes are one-mutation step neighbours
visual_test_df <- visual_landscape(scapes_combined,
                 n = 2,
                  c = 1,
                 s = 1) # this is how I get the transitions between metagenotypes

 peaks_nkc_rep_temp <- peakfinder_NKC(visual_test_df)
 
 temp_df <- data.frame(n = 2,
                       k = 1,
                       c = 1,
                       c_rep = rep,
                       no_peaks = c(nrow(peaks_nkc_rep_temp[[1]]), nrow(peaks_nkc_rep_temp[[2]])),
                       no_peaks_joint = nrow(peaks_nkc_rep_temp[[3]]),
                       max_load = c(max(peaks_nkc_rep_temp[[3]][, "rank_sp1"]), max(peaks_nkc_rep_temp[[3]][, "rank_sp2"])))
 
 peaks_replicated <- rbind(peaks_replicated, temp_df) 
 
}
  
}
```

# (iv) path repeatability
The output of simulation for each combination of N, K, C results in a list of (1) a dataset with endpoint stats of adaptive walks, (2) + (3) interaction matrices for intra- and intergenomic interactions, (4) the landscape replicates, (5) all adaptive walks

Access to the adaptive walks is output[[5]][[k_rep]][[c_rep]][[landscape replicate]][[type of adaptive walk]][[walk replicate]][[species]]
The types of adaptive walks are (1) greedy, (2) random, and (3) true

## NKC paths -> redo some simulations on existing landscapes
```{r}

# for each landscape find metagenotype with lowest fitness and perfomr random walks

# N = 2, K = 0, C = 0
min_walks_nkc_200 <- list()
walk_entropy_nkc_200 <- NULL

set.seed(131313)
for (i in 1:1){ # for each intergenomic IM
  
  min_walks_nkc_200[[i]] <- list()
  
  for (j in 1:100) { # for 10 landscape replicates
    
    temp_landscape <- peaks_nkcs_2001[[4]][[1]][[i]][[j]][[1]] # I'll just look at one species
    min_rank <- rownames(temp_landscape[temp_landscape$rank == max(temp_landscape$rank), ])
    
    min_rank <- as.numeric(min_rank[[1]]) # just pick one in case of neutral plateau
    
    start_meta <- temp_landscape[min_rank, c("F.1", "F.2", "P.1", "P.2")]
    
    min_walks_nkc_200[[i]][[j]] <- list()
    
    for (rep in 1:20){ # replicate it 20 times
    min_walk <- adaptive_walk_R(peaks_nkcs_2001[[4]][[1]][[i]][[j]],
                                walk = "random", 
                                n = 2,
                                c = 0,
                                s = 1,
                                s_tot = 2,
                                IM_c = peaks_nkcs_2001[[3]][[i]][[1]],
                                R = 1,
                                lambda_R = NA,
                                start = "S",
                                desired_start = start_meta,
                                max_steps = 300)[[1]]
    
    min_walk$walk_rep <- rep
    min_walks_nkc_200[[i]][[j]][[rep]] <- min_walk
    
    }
    
    walks = lapply(min_walks_nkc_200[[i]][[j]], "[", , "rank")
    
    walks_strings <- lapply(walks, paste0, collapse = "")
    walks_strings <- unlist(walks_strings)
    
    table_strings <- as.data.frame(table(walks_strings))
    table_strings$ent <- (table_strings$Freq/20)*log2(table_strings$Freq/20)
    
    temp_df <- data.frame(n = 2,
                          k = 0,
                          c = 0,
                          c_rep = i,
                          scape_rep = j,
                          walk_ent = -sum(table_strings$ent),
                          unique_paths = nrow(table_strings),
                          prob_twice_path = sum((table_strings$Freq/20)^2))
    
    walk_entropy_nkc_200 <- rbind(walk_entropy_nkc_200, temp_df) 

    }
    
}
```

```{r}
# for each landscape find metagenotype with lowest fitness and perfomr random walks

# N = 4, K = 0, Ke = 0
min_walks_nkke_400 <- list()
walk_entropy_nkke_400 <- NULL

set.seed(131313)
for (i in 1:1){ # for each IM
  
  min_walks_nkke_400[[i]] <- list()
  
  for (j in 1:100) { # for 10 landscape replicates
    
    temp_landscape <- peaks_nkke_400[[3]][[i]][[j]] 
    min_rank <- temp_landscape[temp_landscape$E1.rank == max(temp_landscape$E1.rank), "E1.rank"] # I'll just look at one environment
    
    min_rank <- as.numeric(min_rank[[1]]) 
    
    start_meta <- temp_landscape[temp_landscape$E1.rank == min_rank, c("F.1", "F.2", "P.1", "P.2")][,1] # just pick one in case of neutral plateau
    
    min_walks_nkke_400[[i]][[j]] <- list()
    
    for (rep in 1:20){ # replicate it 20 times
    min_walk <- adaptive_walk_sea(peaks_nkke_400[[3]][[i]][[j]],
                                walk = "random",
                                n = 2,
                                env_tot = 2,
                                change = 1,
                                lambda_change = NA,
                                start = "S",
                                desired_start = start_meta,
                                max_steps = 300)
    
    min_walk$walk_rep <- rep
    min_walks_nkke_400[[i]][[j]][[rep]] <- min_walk
    
    }
    
    walks = lapply(min_walks_nkke_400[[i]][[j]], "[", , "E1.rank")
    
    walks_strings <- lapply(walks, paste0, collapse = "")
    walks_strings <- unlist(walks_strings)
    
    table_strings <- as.data.frame(table(walks_strings))
    table_strings$ent <- (table_strings$Freq/20)*log2(table_strings$Freq/20)
    
    temp_df <- data.frame(n = 4,
                          k = 0,
                          ke = 0,
                          IM_rep = i,
                          scape_rep = j,
                          walk_ent = -sum(table_strings$ent),
                          unique_paths = nrow(table_strings),
                          prob_twice_path = sum((table_strings$Freq/20)^2))
    
    walk_entropy_nkke_400 <- rbind(walk_entropy_nkke_400, temp_df) 

    }
    
}
```

```{r}
    min_rank <- as.numeric(min_rank[[1]]) # just pick one in case of neutral plateau
    
    start_meta <- c(temp_landscape[min_rank, c("F.1", "F.2", "F.3", "F.4")], temp_landscape[min_rank, c("F.1", "F.2", "F.3", "F.4")]) # the second part does not matter
    
    min_walks_nkc_400[[i]][[j]] <- list()
    
    for (rep in 1:20){ # replicate it 20 times
    min_walk <- adaptive_walk_R(peaks_nkcs_4001[[4]][[i]][[1]][[j]],
                                walk = "random", 
                                n = 4,
                                c = 0,
                                s = 0,
                                s_tot = 2,
                                IM_c = peaks_nkcs_4001[[3]][[i]][[1]],
                                R = 1,
                                lambda_R = NA,
                                start = "S",
                                desired_start = start_meta,
                                max_steps = 300)[[1]]
    
    min_walk$walk_rep <- rep
    min_walks_nkc_400[[i]][[j]][[rep]] <- min_walk
    
    }
    
    walks = lapply(min_walks_nkc_400[[i]][[j]], "[", , "rank")
    
    walks_strings <- lapply(walks, paste0, collapse = "")
    walks_strings <- unlist(walks_strings)

                          unique_paths = nrow(table_strings),
                          prob_twice_path = sum((table_strings$Freq/20)^2))
    
    walk_entropy_nkc_400 <- rbind(walk_entropy_nkc_400, temp_df) 

    }
    
}

# N = 4, K = 1
min_walks_nkc_410 <- list()
walk_entropy_nkc_410 <- NULL

set.seed(131313)
for (i in 1:5){ # for each intragenomic IM
  
  min_walks_nkc_410[[i]] <- list()
  
  for (j in 1:20) { # for 10 landscape replicates
    
    temp_landscape <- peaks_nkcs_4101[[4]][[i]][[1]][[j]][[1]] # I'll just look at one species
    min_rank <- rownames(temp_landscape[temp_landscape$rank == max(temp_landscape$rank), ])
    
    min_rank <- as.numeric(min_rank[[1]]) # just pick one in case of neutral plateau
    
    start_meta <- c(temp_landscape[min_rank, c("F.1", "F.2", "F.3", "F.4")], temp_landscape[min_rank, c("F.1", "F.2", "F.3", "F.4")]) # the second part does not matter
    
    min_walks_nkc_410[[i]][[j]] <- list()
    
    for (rep in 1:20){ # replicate it 20 times
    min_walk <- adaptive_walk_R(peaks_nkcs_4101[[4]][[i]][[1]][[j]],
                                walk = "random", 
                                n = 4,
                                c = 0,
                                s = 0,
                                s_tot = 2,
                                IM_c = peaks_nkcs_4101[[3]][[i]][[1]],
                                R = 1,
                                lambda_R = NA,
                                start = "S",
                                desired_start = start_meta,
                                max_steps = 300)[[1]]
    
    min_walk$walk_rep <- rep
    min_walks_nkc_410[[i]][[j]][[rep]] <- min_walk
    
    }
    
    walks = lapply(min_walks_nkc_410[[i]][[j]], "[", , "rank")
    
    walks_strings <- lapply(walks, paste0, collapse = "")
    walks_strings <- unlist(walks_strings)
    
    table_strings <- as.data.frame(table(walks_strings))
    table_strings$ent <- (table_strings$Freq/20)*log2(table_strings$Freq/20)
    
    temp_df <- data.frame(n = 4,
                          k = 1,
                          c = 0,
                          k_rep = i,
                          scape_rep = j,
                          walk_ent = -sum(table_strings$ent),
                          unique_paths = nrow(table_strings),
                          prob_twice_path = sum((table_strings$Freq/20)^2))
    
    walk_entropy_nkc_410 <- rbind(walk_entropy_nkc_410, temp_df) 

    }
    
}
```

### Fig. no. outcomes/landscape
````{r}
no_paths_NK <- ggplot(walk_entropy_df_NK,
       aes(y = unique_paths,
           x = interaction(k,c,n),
           group = interaction(k,c,n))) +
  geom_jitter(col = "chartreuse4", # for equilibrium points
              size = 3,
              height = 0.01,
              alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_violin(col = "grey30",
              fill = "transparent") +
  stat_summary(fun = mean,
               geom = "crossbar", # adds the mean proportion for each rank/landscape
               linewidth = 0.4,
               col = "black") +
  stat_summary(fun = median,
               geom = "point", # adds the median proportion for each rank/landscape
               shape = 18,
               size = 3,
               col = "black") +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Paths/landscape",
                     limits = c(0.99,20.01),
                     breaks = seq(1,20,2)) +
   scale_x_discrete(labels=c("0.0.4" = "4-0",
                            "1.0.4" = "4-1",
                            "2.0.4" = "4-2",
                            "3.0.4" = "4-3")) +
  xlab(expression(italic(N*"'"-K*"'"))) +
  theme_bw() +
  fig_theme

````

### Fig. Entropy
````{r}
# entropy
path_entropy_fig_NK <- ggplot(walk_entropy_df_NK,
       aes(x = interaction(k,c,n),
           y = walk_ent,
           group = interaction(k,c,n))) +
  geom_jitter(col = "chartreuse4",
              size = 2.5,
              height = 0.01,
              alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_violin(col = "grey30",
              fill = "transparent") +
  stat_summary(fun = median,
               geom = "point", # adds the median proportion for each rank/landscape
               shape = 18,
               size = 3,
               col = "black") +
  stat_summary(fun = mean,
               geom = "crossbar", # adds the mean proportion for each rank/landscape
               linewidth = 0.4,
               col = "black") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels=c("0.0.4" = "4-0",
                            "1.0.4" = "4-1",
                            "2.0.4" = "4-2",
                            "3.0.4" = "4-3")) +
  xlab(expression(italic(N*"'"-K*"'"))) +
  ylab("Shannon entropy") +
  ylim(c(-0.01,4.5)) +

  fig_theme

```` 

### Fig. probability of reaching the same outcome twice
````{r}
reaching_path_fig_NK <- ggplot(walk_entropy_df_NK,
       aes(x = interaction(k,c,n),
           y = prob_twice_path,
           group = interaction(k,c,n))) +
  geom_jitter(col = "chartreuse4",
              size = 2.5,
              height = 0.01,
              alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_violin(col = "grey30",
              fill = "transparent") +
  stat_summary(fun = median,
               geom = "point", # adds the median proportion for each rank/landscape
               shape = 18,
               size = 3,
               col = "black") +
  stat_summary(fun = mean,
               geom = "crossbar", # adds the mean proportion for each rank/landscape
               linewidth = 0.4,
               col = "black") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels=c("0.0.4" = "4-0",
                            "1.0.4" = "4-1",
                            "2.0.4" = "4-2",
                            "3.0.4" = "4-3")) +
  xlab(expression(italic(N*"'"-K*"'"))) +
  ylab("Probability of same path") +
  ylim(c(-0.01,1.01)) +
  theme_bw() +
  fig_theme
````
